d1: The binding identifies the target and requested color, but its identity criterion is underspecified and invites inconsistent judgments: traces agree it turns brown, yet split on whether the visible hollow top means it is no longer the same cylinder. Refine the decision logic to distinguish observable evidence of a different object from a changed appearance, and to assess identity using the source-to-edit correspondence and stable features (location among the objects, approximate size, upright cylindrical form), without treating the hollow-looking top alone as decisive or ignoring it. Keep brownness and identity as separate checks, then apply the rubric’s partial-progress rule: a completed color change with genuinely unresolved identity is not automatically “no”; reserve failure for clear evidence the target was replaced or no requested change occurred, and use unresolved when the images cannot establish identity. The traces are valid observed executions with no dependency or transport failures, so this is a semantic/criterion-calibration issue. Their high-confidence disagreement despite the same evidence signals that the criterion needs clearer evidence thresholds, not that confidence should be lowered or the identity requirement removed.
